Which question is each country the subject of?

Two maps of the same corpus. The first asks what a country was discussed as; the second asks who was in the room. Hover anything shaded on the first map to see the entries it carries, and click through to one.

Topic entries on the map

Shading is the number of meetings the corpus holds on that country's questions — Council and Assembly together. A country is shaded because an entry is about it, a curated judgement recorded in build_topics.py, not a count of times its name appears in a vote record.

meetings per country 0

Hover a shaded country for its entries · click to open one · drag and scroll to move around the map

Entries with no country

Some entries are about a regime or an institution rather than a place, so they appear on no polygon.

The other question

Who was in the room

Who sat at the table, who was invited into the chamber, and who voted against. Switch the metric to redraw the map; the table at the foot of the page ranks every state on all of them at once.

This second half of the page is essentially about the Security Council. The Assembly JSON records only the presiding country for each meeting — no member or invited lists — and holds just 929 country-level vote records. The map and the table are therefore built almost entirely from Council data ( member appearances, invitations, presidencies). Reading this page as a portrait of the Assembly would be wrong.

0

Shading is a continuous magnitude on a single-hue ramp, light to dark. Grey means no record under that metric. Historical entities — the USSR, Yugoslavia, Zaire — keep their own identity in the table but borrow their successor's polygon to appear on the map at all; that is a compromise for drawing, not a claim that the two are the same. Six states (Maldives, Monaco, San Marino, Saint Kitts and Nevis, Nauru, Marshall Islands) have no polygon in the basemap, so they appear in the table but cannot be shaded.

Every state and entity

All of them, on every metric at once. Click a column to sort; Discussed as links to the entries that country carries. That column is a join through the basemap polygon, so historical entities borrowing a successor's polygon — the USSR, Zaire — are left blank rather than credited with a question that postdates them.

The corpus contains 439 distinct country strings, 209 of which occur three times or fewer and are mostly OCR noise (Aus t r a l i a, Fran~e). After normalisation of country records resolve; the remaining are unresolvable or are not states at all (the PLO, the Secretary-General) and are excluded.
